Create a resource by name.

A project registers the git repository at --path in the current group, which must exist unless it is the default group. A group is created empty and holds the projects you register with --group later.

With --from-dir DIR in place of NAME, create project registers every git repository at DIR or under it, down to --depth levels. Each project is named after its directory, lowercased with each run of characters other than ASCII letters, digits and dashes made one dash, and records its path and the URL of its origin without any credentials; the checked-out branch is not recorded. A path the group already holds is reported unchanged, so running it again adds only new clones.

Use --dry-run to check the arguments without writing anything, and -o yaml with it to print the manifest instead, ready for apply -f.

Resource types: projects (project, proj) and groups (group). Type words are case-insensitive.

Examples:
  # Register the repository at ~/dev/hldr as a project in the current group
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr'

  # Register a project in the work group with two labels
  slipway create project api --path '~/work/api' -n work --label lang=go --label tier=api

  # Register a project with the remote and the branch it is expected to have
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --remote git@github.com:hvpaiva/hldr.git --branch main

  # Create a group with a description
  slipway create group work --description "Projects for the day job"

  # Check the arguments without writing the project
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --dry-run

  # Print the manifest of a project without registering it
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --dry-run -o yaml

  # Register every repository in ~/dev/personal in the personal group
  slipway create project --from-dir ~/dev/personal -n personal

  # Write the manifests of the repositories two levels under ~/work to a file
  slipway create project --from-dir ~/work --depth 2 --dry-run -o yaml > work.yaml

Options:
      --path DIR           Directory of the git repository to register; required for a project given by NAME. A relative directory is stored resolved against the current directory, a ~ path as written.
      --description TEXT   A short description of the resource.
      --label KEY=VALUE    A label to set on the new resource; may be repeated.
      --remote URL         The URL the origin remote is expected to have, written to spec.remote. A URL that embeds credentials is refused; use a credential helper.
      --branch NAME        The branch the project is expected to have checked out, written to spec.branch.
      --from-dir DIR       Register every git repository at or under DIR as a project, in place of NAME.
      --depth N            How many directory levels under --from-dir to search, from 1 to 8. The search stops at a repository and never follows a symbolic link under --from-dir. (default 1)
      --dry-run            Print what would change and write nothing.
  -o, --output FORMAT      Output format; without it, each resource prints a result line such as project/hldr created. One of: json, yaml, name.

Usage:
  slipway create (TYPE NAME | project --from-dir DIR) [flags]

Use "slipway --help" for a list of global options (applies to all commands).
